column1: Node tables, edge tables, and MATCH were introduced in SQL Server {{c1::2017}}.
column2:
SQL Server 2017 supports fixed graph patterns with MATCH. Variable-length shortest paths arrived in a later version.
Review source

column1: SHORTEST_PATH requires SQL Server {{c1::2019}} or later.
column2:
SQL Server 2017 has basic graph tables and MATCH, but that does not make SHORTEST_PATH available there.
Review source

column1: Create a graph entity table with CREATE TABLE dbo.Person (PersonID INT PRIMARY KEY) {{c1::AS NODE}};
column2:
AS NODE lets SQL Server generate the graph identifier. The declared PersonID remains a separate application key.
CREATE TABLE dbo.Person (PersonID int PRIMARY KEY, Name nvarchar(100)) AS NODE;
Review source

column1: Create a relationship table with CREATE TABLE dbo.Knows (ConnectionDate DATE) {{c1::AS EDGE}};
column2:
AS EDGE supplies the graph fields for the endpoints. ConnectionDate is an additional attribute of the relationship.
CREATE TABLE dbo.Knows (ConnectionDate date) AS EDGE;
Review source

column1: SQL Server exposes each node's graph identifier through the {{c1::$node_id}} pseudo-column.
column2:
$node_id is the graph identity used by edges. The application can still use PersonID for ordinary lookups.
INSERT INTO dbo.Knows ($from_id, $to_id)
SELECT a.$node_id, b.$node_id
FROM dbo.Person AS a, dbo.Person AS b
WHERE a.PersonID = 1 AND b.PersonID = 2;
Review source

column1: The automatically generated {{c1::$edge_id}} pseudo-column identifies an edge.
column2:
The identifier belongs to the relationship row itself. Its endpoint identities live in separate pseudo-columns.
SELECT $edge_id, $from_id, $to_id FROM dbo.Knows;
Review source

column1: An edge's {{c1::$from_id}} stores the graph identifier of its originating node.
column2:
For Alice knows Bob, this field holds Alice's graph ID. The destination goes in $to_id.
INSERT INTO dbo.Knows ($from_id, $to_id)
SELECT a.$node_id, b.$node_id
FROM dbo.Person AS a, dbo.Person AS b
WHERE a.PersonID = 1 AND b.PersonID = 2;
Review source

column1: An edge's {{c1::$to_id}} stores the graph identifier of its destination node.
column2:
For Alice knows Bob, this field holds Bob's graph ID. The origin goes in $from_id.
INSERT INTO dbo.Knows ($from_id, $to_id)
SELECT a.$node_id, b.$node_id
FROM dbo.Person AS a, dbo.Person AS b
WHERE a.PersonID = 1 AND b.PersonID = 2;
Review source

column1: A graph pattern is placed in a SELECT filter as WHERE {{c1::MATCH}}(a-(e)->b).
column2:
Declare a and b as node aliases and e as an edge alias. MATCH then specifies how they must connect.
SELECT a.PersonID, b.PersonID
FROM dbo.Person AS a, dbo.Knows AS e, dbo.Person AS b
WHERE MATCH(a-(e)->b);
Review source

column1: For an edge from a to b, use MATCH(a-(e){{c1::->}}b).
column2:
The right arrow means e starts at a and ends at b. Reversing the arrow changes which orientation the query matches.
SELECT a.PersonID, b.PersonID
FROM dbo.Person AS a, dbo.Knows AS e, dbo.Person AS b
WHERE MATCH(a-(e)->b);
Review source

column1: For an edge from b to a, use MATCH(a{{c1::<-}}(e)-b).
column2:
The left arrow means e starts at b and ends at a. The pattern reads the existing edge without changing it.
SELECT a.PersonID, b.PersonID
FROM dbo.Person AS a, dbo.Knows AS e, dbo.Person AS b
WHERE MATCH(a<-(e)-b);
Review source

column1: To reach p3 via p2 using edge aliases k1 and k2: MATCH(p1-(k1)->p2{{c1::-(k2)->p3}}).
column2:
The first hop ends at p2, and the second starts there. Distinct edge aliases let the steps refer to different edge rows.
SELECT p1.PersonID, p3.PersonID
FROM dbo.Person AS p1, dbo.Knows AS k1,
     dbo.Person AS p2, dbo.Knows AS k2, dbo.Person AS p3
WHERE MATCH(p1-(k1)->p2-(k2)->p3)
  AND p3.PersonID <> p1.PersonID;
Review source

column1: Add an ordinary attribute filter with WHERE MATCH(a-(e)->b) {{c1::AND}} a.Department = b.Department.
column2:
The MATCH predicate tests connectivity. The separate AND condition tests a regular column on the matched nodes.
SELECT a.PersonID, b.PersonID
FROM dbo.Person AS a, dbo.Knows AS e, dbo.Person AS b
WHERE MATCH(a-(e)->b)
  AND a.Department = b.Department;
Review source

column1: Mark a repeated edge table in FROM as dbo.Knows {{c1::FOR PATH}} AS e.
column2:
Mark the repeated node alias too. A graph-path aggregate can then summarize attributes across the repeated steps.
SELECT s.PersonID,
       STRING_AGG(n.Name, ' -> ') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Path,
       LAST_VALUE(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Destination,
       COUNT(n.PersonID) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Hops,
       COUNT(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS NamedVisits
FROM dbo.Person AS s, dbo.Knows FOR PATH AS e,
     dbo.Person FOR PATH AS n
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(s(-(e)->n)+));
-- PersonID is non-NULL; NamedVisits excludes NULL names.
Review source

column1: A variable-length search nests the function as WHERE MATCH({{c1::SHORTEST_PATH}}(s(-(e)->n)+)).
column2:
The function asks for a shortest match of the repeated directed pattern. Shortest means fewest hops.
SELECT s.PersonID,
       STRING_AGG(n.Name, ' -> ') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Path,
       LAST_VALUE(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Destination,
       COUNT(n.PersonID) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Hops,
       COUNT(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS NamedVisits
FROM dbo.Person AS s, dbo.Knows FOR PATH AS e,
     dbo.Person FOR PATH AS n
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(s(-(e)->n)+));
-- PersonID is non-NULL; NamedVisits excludes NULL names.
Review source

column1: In SHORTEST_PATH(s(-(e)->n){{c1::+}}), the repeated pattern occurs one or more times.
column2:
The plus requires at least one edge traversal in this pattern. The starting node alone does not count as a match.
SELECT s.PersonID,
       STRING_AGG(n.Name, ' -> ') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Path,
       LAST_VALUE(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Destination,
       COUNT(n.PersonID) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Hops,
       COUNT(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS NamedVisits
FROM dbo.Person AS s, dbo.Knows FOR PATH AS e,
     dbo.Person FOR PATH AS n
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(s(-(e)->n)+));
-- PersonID is non-NULL; NamedVisits excludes NULL names.
Review source

column1: For one to three repetitions, use SHORTEST_PATH(s(-(e)->n){{c1::{1,3}}}).
column2:
The lower bound excludes a start-only path. The upper bound limits this one-edge pattern to three hops.
SELECT s.PersonID,
       STRING_AGG(n.Name, ' -> ') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Path,
       LAST_VALUE(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Destination,
       COUNT(n.PersonID) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Hops,
       COUNT(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS NamedVisits
FROM dbo.Person AS s, dbo.Knows FOR PATH AS e,
     dbo.Person FOR PATH AS n
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(s(-(e)->n){1,3}));
-- PersonID is non-NULL; NamedVisits excludes NULL names.
Review source

column1: The graph-path aggregate clause is LAST_VALUE(n.Name) {{c1::WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH)}}.
column2:
This form aggregates values across the matched path. The ordinary window-function form does not read graph-path collections.
SELECT s.PersonID,
       STRING_AGG(n.Name, ' -> ') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Path,
       LAST_VALUE(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Destination,
       COUNT(n.PersonID) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Hops,
       COUNT(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS NamedVisits
FROM dbo.Person AS s, dbo.Knows FOR PATH AS e,
     dbo.Person FOR PATH AS n
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(s(-(e)->n)+));
-- PersonID is non-NULL; NamedVisits excludes NULL names.
Review source

column1: Concatenate visited node names with {{c1::STRING_AGG}}(n.Name, ' -> ') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH).
column2:
The result joins names in path order using the supplied separator. NULL names do not add a name to the string.
SELECT s.PersonID,
       STRING_AGG(n.Name, ' -> ') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Path,
       LAST_VALUE(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Destination,
       COUNT(n.PersonID) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Hops,
       COUNT(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS NamedVisits
FROM dbo.Person AS s, dbo.Knows FOR PATH AS e,
     dbo.Person FOR PATH AS n
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(s(-(e)->n)+));
-- PersonID is non-NULL; NamedVisits excludes NULL names.
Review source

column1: Project the final visited node's name with {{c1::LAST_VALUE}}(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH).
column2:
LAST_VALUE picks a node's final value in path order. It does not accept an attribute of the repeated edge.
SELECT s.PersonID,
       STRING_AGG(n.Name, ' -> ') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Path,
       LAST_VALUE(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Destination,
       COUNT(n.PersonID) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Hops,
       COUNT(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS NamedVisits
FROM dbo.Person AS s, dbo.Knows FOR PATH AS e,
     dbo.Person FOR PATH AS n
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(s(-(e)->n)+));
-- PersonID is non-NULL; NamedVisits excludes NULL names.
Review source

column1: For s(-(e)->n)+ with n.ID NOT NULL, {{c1::COUNT}}(n.ID) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) counts hops.
column2:
Each step supplies one value of n.ID. Because that ID cannot be NULL, none of the hops are skipped.
SELECT s.PersonID,
       STRING_AGG(n.Name, ' -> ') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Path,
       LAST_VALUE(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Destination,
       COUNT(n.PersonID) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Hops,
       COUNT(n.Name) WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS NamedVisits
FROM dbo.Person AS s, dbo.Knows FOR PATH AS e,
     dbo.Person FOR PATH AS n
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(s(-(e)->n)+));
-- PersonID is non-NULL; NamedVisits excludes NULL names.
Review source

column1: Graph-path COUNT requires an {{c1::expression}} rather than *.
column2:
